stories.title: 早上的一杯茶
stories.summary: A quiet start to Lin An’s day.

paragraphs.translation: This morning, Lin An got up very early. She walked to the kitchen and made herself a cup of tea.
It was raining lightly outside, but the room was peaceful. She drank tea while planning her day.

quiz.question: What was the weather like?
quiz.explanation: 窗外下着小雨 means that light rain was falling outside.

stories.title: 今天吃什么？
stories.summary: Two friends solve the daily lunch question.

paragraphs.translation: At noon, Xiao Yu and Daming were both hungry. They stood outside the office and discussed what to eat.
Xiao Yu wanted noodles, while Daming wanted rice. Then they saw a small restaurant that had both.

quiz.question: Why did the small restaurant suit both friends?
quiz.explanation: The restaurant had both foods: 两种都有。

stories.title: 坐错车了
stories.summary: A small mistake becomes a useful conversation.

paragraphs.translation: Chen Fei wanted to go to the museum, but he boarded the wrong bus. After ten minutes, the road looked unfamiliar.
He asked the driver for help. The driver smiled and told him to get off at the next stop and take bus number eight back.

quiz.question: What did the driver tell Chen Fei to do first?
options: Get off at the next stop
quiz.explanation: The driver first said 下一站下车 — get off at the next stop.

stories.title: 周末的小市场
stories.summary: Mei discovers a friendly neighbourhood market.

paragraphs.translation: Every Saturday, there is a small market near Mei’s home. Vegetables, fruit, flowers, and handmade bread are sold there.
Mei bought three red apples. The seller gave her one small pear and said, “Try this—it’s very sweet!”

quiz.question: What extra fruit did the seller give Mei?
quiz.explanation: 老板又送给她一个小梨 means the seller also gave her a small pear.

stories.title: 四个声调
stories.summary: Hear how mā, má, mǎ and mà change a word's meaning.

coach.title: Meet the four tones
notes: Pinyin uses letters to show pronunciation. The mark above the main vowel shows the tone: mā, má, mǎ, mà.
1st tone stays high and level; 2nd rises; 3rd is low (often dipping then rising when said on its own); 4th falls sharply.
Play each example separately, then repeat it. Keep the vowel sound similar and change the pitch. These are different words, not four ways to say the same word.

paragraphs.translation: Xiao An is learning pinyin. There are four characters in the book: mum, hemp, horse and scold.
The teacher says, “Listen first, then say it.” Xiao An listens again and reads slowly.

quiz.question: Which pinyin means “horse”?
quiz.explanation: 马 is mǎ, with a third-tone mark. Changing the tone can change the meaning.

stories.title: 买还是卖？
stories.summary: Practise mǎi and mài at a fruit stall.

coach.title: Third tone or fourth tone?
notes: 买 mǎi means “buy”; 卖 mài means “sell”. Their initial m and final ai match, but their tones differ.
Say mǎi low; when practising it alone, let it dip and rise. Say mài with a firm falling pitch.
Read the small mark over a: ǎ versus à. Listen, repeat, and then use the word in a sentence.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hello! I want to buy apples.

paragraphs.speaker: Seller
paragraphs.translation: I sell apples. How many would you like?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: I'd like three. Thank you!

quiz.question: Which word would a customer use for “buy”?
quiz.explanation: The customer 买 mǎi (buys); the seller 卖 mài (sells).

stories.title: 四个，不是十个
stories.summary: A dumpling order helps you compare sì and shí.

coach.title: Hear s and sh
notes: 四 sì means four; 十 shí means ten. Both the initial sound and the tone change.
For s, keep your tongue near the front behind the teeth. For sh, move the tongue tip back toward the ridge behind the teeth; avoid pressing it against the palate.
Don't read pinyin like English spelling. Listen to the complete syllables sì and shí, then practise the order below.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hello! I'd like four steamed buns.

paragraphs.speaker: Server
paragraphs.translation: Ten?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Four, not ten. Thank you!

quiz.question: How many buns does the customer want?
quiz.explanation: The customer corrects the order: 四个，不是十个 — four, not ten.

stories.title: 你好吗？
stories.englishTitle: A Little Question, a Light Tone
stories.summary: Meet the neutral tone in a friendly greeting.

coach.title: Keep the last syllable light
notes: 吗 ma is a question particle. Its neutral tone has no tone mark: keep it short and light, rather than giving it a fixed full tone.
In 谢谢 xièxie, the second xie is also light. Compare it with the marked first syllable.
Pinyin usually writes 你好 as nǐ hǎo. In speech, the first third tone changes to a rising tone before the next third tone. Listen for ní hǎo, while remembering the usual written form.

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: Hello! How are you?

paragraphs.speaker: B
paragraphs.translation: I'm very well, thank you. And you?

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: I'm well too. See you tomorrow!

quiz.question: Why does ma in nǐ hǎo ma have no tone mark?
options: It has a light neutral tone
quiz.explanation: 吗 ma is neutral-toned here: it is shorter and lighter than a full-tone syllable.

stories.title: 很高兴认识你
stories.summary: Introduce yourself and ask someone's name.

coach.title: A conversation you can reuse
notes: 我叫… means “My name is…”. Replace the example name with your own.
你叫什么名字？ asks “What's your name?”. Finish with 很高兴认识你 — “Nice to meet you”.

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao An
paragraphs.translation: Hello! My name is Xiao An. What's your name?

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao Lin
paragraphs.translation: My name is Xiao Lin. Nice to meet you!

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao An
paragraphs.translation: I'm happy to meet you too. Do you live nearby?

paragraphs.speaker: Xiao Lin
paragraphs.translation: Yes, I live nearby.

quiz.question: Which phrase introduces your name?
quiz.explanation: Use 我叫… followed by your name. 你叫什么名字？ is the question you can ask in return.

stories.title: 一杯热茶
stories.summary: Order tea, choose hot or iced, and ask the price.

coach.title: Make a simple order
notes: 我想要… means “I'd like…”. 一杯 yì bēi is “one cup”. Try changing 茶 to 咖啡.
热的还是冰的？ offers a choice: “Hot or iced?”. 多少钱？ asks “How much?”.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hello! I'd like a cup of tea.

paragraphs.speaker: Server
paragraphs.translation: Hot or iced?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Hot, please. How much is it?

paragraphs.speaker: Server
paragraphs.translation: Ten yuan. Please wait a moment.

quiz.question: What does the customer order?
quiz.explanation: The customer asks for 一杯茶 (a cup of tea), then chooses 热的 (hot).

stories.title: 需要袋子吗？
stories.summary: Handle a price, a shopping bag, and payment.

coach.title: Useful checkout phrases
notes: 需要…吗？ asks “Do you need…?”. 不需要 means “don't need”.
可以…吗？ asks whether something is allowed or possible. 可以刷卡吗？ means “Can I pay by card?”.

paragraphs.speaker: Cashier
paragraphs.translation: That's twenty yuan in total. Do you need a bag?

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: No, thank you. I have a bag.

paragraphs.speaker: Customer
paragraphs.translation: Can I pay by card?

paragraphs.speaker: Cashier
paragraphs.translation: Yes. Thank you, goodbye!

quiz.question: Why doesn't the customer need a bag?
options: The customer has a bag already
quiz.explanation: 我有袋子 means “I have a bag”.

stories.title: 地铁站在哪里？
stories.summary: Ask where something is and follow simple directions.

coach.title: Ask, then listen for direction words
notes: 请问 is a polite way to get someone's attention before asking a question.
…在哪里？ means “Where is…?”. Listen for 一直走 (go straight), 左转 (turn left), and 右边 (on the right).

paragraphs.speaker: Visitor
paragraphs.translation: Excuse me, where is the metro station?

paragraphs.speaker: Local
paragraphs.translation: Go straight, then turn left. The station is on the right.

paragraphs.speaker: Visitor
paragraphs.translation: Is it far from here?

paragraphs.speaker: Local
paragraphs.translation: Not far. It's a five-minute walk.

quiz.question: What should the visitor do after going straight?
quiz.explanation: 然后左转 means “then turn left”. The station itself is on the right after that turn.

stories.title: 明天有空吗？
stories.summary: Invite a friend and agree on a time and place.

coach.title: Make an invitation
notes: 你明天有空吗？ asks “Are you free tomorrow?”. 一起…吧 is a friendly suggestion: “Let's… together”.
几点？ asks “What time?”. Practise changing 下午三点 to a different meeting time.

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: Are you free tomorrow? Let's have tea together.

paragraphs.speaker: B
paragraphs.translation: Sure! What time?

paragraphs.speaker: A
paragraphs.translation: Three in the afternoon. Let's meet at the café.

paragraphs.speaker: B
paragraphs.translation: Okay. See you tomorrow!

quiz.question: When will the friends meet?
quiz.explanation: They are making plans for 明天 (tomorrow), at 下午三点 (3 p.m.).

stories.title: 请再说一遍
stories.summary: Keep a conversation going when you don't understand.

coach.title: A useful rescue phrase
notes: 不好意思 politely softens a request: “Excuse me / sorry”. 我没听懂 means “I didn't understand what I heard”.
请再说一遍 means “Please say it again”. 请说慢一点 asks someone to slow down. Try saying both without looking.

paragraphs.speaker: Shop assistant
paragraphs.translation: This is fifteen yuan.

paragraphs.speaker: Learner
paragraphs.translation: Sorry, I didn't understand. Please say it again.

paragraphs.speaker: Learner
paragraphs.translation: Please speak a little slower.

paragraphs.speaker: Shop assistant
paragraphs.translation: Sure. Fifteen yuan.

quiz.question: Which phrase asks someone to repeat?
options: 请再说一遍 qǐng zài shuō yí biàn
quiz.explanation: 请再说一遍 means “Please say it again”. Add 请说慢一点 if you also need a slower pace.

stories.title: 你更喜欢老车还是新车？
stories.summary: Start a friendly car-meet chat and compare what you value.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 你更喜欢 A 还是 B？ asks which you prefer. Use 对我来说… (“for me…”) to give a personal reason rather than declare a winner.
原厂 means factory specification; 改装 means modified. Here 老款天际线 refers to an older Nissan Skyline, while 新款丰田八六 is casual speech for a newer Toyota GR86, not the older AE86.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Is this old car yours? Have you modified it?

paragraphs.speaker: Owner
paragraphs.translation: Yes. The engine is still factory specification; I only changed the wheels.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Do you prefer older cars or newer ones?

paragraphs.speaker: Owner
paragraphs.translation: I like the mechanical feel of older Skylines, but I commute in a newer Toyota GR86.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: For me, being comfortable to drive matters more. May I take a photo?

paragraphs.speaker: Owner
paragraphs.translation: Of course! Just please keep the licence plate out of the photo.

quiz.question: What has the owner changed?
quiz.explanation: 只换了轮圈 means only the wheel rims were changed.

stories.title: 日规车不等于日系车
stories.englishTitle: Japanese-market Is Not the Same as Japanese-brand
stories.summary: Learn the distinction behind JDM, a Japanese brand, and where a car was built.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: JDM means Japanese Domestic Market. 日规车 is the useful Chinese expression for a car specified for Japan’s market; 日系车 refers to a Japanese-brand car.
不一定 means “not necessarily”. A badge, a right-hand steering wheel, or a manufacturing country alone does not establish an individual car’s original market. Check the exact specification.

A separate distinction: the R32 Skyline GT-R used an RB26DETT inline-six; the later R35 GT-R used a VR38DETT V6. Generation, engine layout and original sales market describe different aspects of a car; see Nissan’s history link.

paragraphs.translation: Car fans often talk about Japanese-market cars. This term concerns the market a car was originally intended for.
A Japanese-brand car is not necessarily a Japanese-market version. The same model may have different versions in different countries.
The manufacturing location, brand and original sales market are three different pieces of information.
When chatting, you can ask: “Is this the Japanese-market version?” This is more precise than only asking the brand.

quiz.question: Which fact defines the distinction being discussed?
quiz.explanation: 日规 concerns the Japanese-market specification; 日系 concerns a Japanese brand.

sources.title: Nissan: R32 and R35 history and engine layouts

stories.title: 看车前先问清楚
stories.englishTitle: Before You View a Used Car
stories.summary: Ask about records, modifications and an independent inspection.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 有没有…？ is a natural way to ask whether something exists. Ask for 保养记录 (“service records”) rather than relying on a reassuring adjective.
方便…吗？ politely asks whether an arrangement works. The dialogue arranges an inspection; it does not treat a seller’s claims as a confirmed mechanical assessment.

paragraphs.speaker: Buyer
paragraphs.translation: Hello, is the car you advertised still available? I would like to view it.

paragraphs.speaker: Seller
paragraphs.translation: Yes. What would you like to know?

paragraphs.speaker: Buyer
paragraphs.translation: Are there service records? Has the engine been modified?

paragraphs.speaker: Seller
paragraphs.translation: There are some records. I will send you the parts list as well.

paragraphs.speaker: Buyer
paragraphs.translation: Thanks. Could we arrange an independent inspection? Would Saturday morning work?

paragraphs.speaker: Seller
paragraphs.translation: That works. Let us confirm the time and location first.

quiz.question: What does the buyer want to arrange?
quiz.explanation: 能安排独立检查吗？ asks whether an independent inspection can be arranged.

stories.title: 涡轮不是凭空变出动力
stories.summary: Connect the words for exhaust, turbine and compressor to a real mechanism.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: A turbo uses exhaust-gas energy to drive a turbine connected to an intake-air compressor. It does not send the exhaust itself into the intake as its normal purpose.
More intake air can support burning more fuel and making more power. 先…再… describes a sequence; 并不 means “does not actually”.

paragraphs.translation: A turbocharger uses energy in exhaust gas. The exhaust first drives the turbine.
The turbine drives a compressor through a shaft. The compressor then pushes more air into the engine.
With suitable fuel delivery, more air can help produce more power. The energy is not created from nothing.
Air heats up when compressed. Many turbocharged cars use an intercooler to cool the intake air.

quiz.question: What normally drives the turbo’s turbine?
quiz.explanation: 废气先推动涡轮: exhaust gas drives the turbine, which drives the compressor.

stories.title: 可以推荐，别剧透
stories.summary: Ask what someone enjoys, describe a show, and avoid spoiling the ending.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 你最近在看什么？ starts a natural chat. 有没有…推荐？ asks for recommendations without requiring a particular title.
剧透 means reveal plot details. 别剧透 is casual and direct; 请不要告诉我结局 is a fuller alternative. Discussing style and pacing can keep a recommendation spoiler-free.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: What anime have you been watching lately? Any recommendations?

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Do you prefer everyday-life shows or action shows?

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Either is fine. I want good characters and pacing that is not too slow.

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Then try this one. I like the art style and the music.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Great, send me the name. But no spoilers—I have not even seen episode one!

quiz.question: Which information would best respect the request?
quiz.explanation: The learner asks for a name and general recommendation, while saying 别剧透.

stories.title: 你看字幕还是配音？
stories.summary: Discuss viewing preferences and turn a familiar scene into listening practice.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 字幕 means subtitles; 配音 means dubbing or voice acting. 原声 refers to the original audio. These are viewing choices, not a ranking of fans.
先…再… gives a practical sequence. The dialogue suggests replaying one familiar scene; it does not require understanding a whole episode immediately.

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Do you watch with subtitles or choose a dubbed version?

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: I usually choose the original audio. But I also want to use Mandarin dubbing to practise listening.

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: You could choose a scene you already know. Watch it once with subtitles first.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Then hide the subtitles and listen again? If I do not understand, can I pause?

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Of course. One useful sentence remembered is better than rushing to the end.

quiz.question: What is suggested for the first viewing?
options: Watch a familiar scene with subtitles
quiz.explanation: 先开着字幕看一遍 means to watch once with subtitles on first.

stories.title: 动画不是每张画都一样重要
stories.summary: Learn the difference between key poses, in-betweens and timing.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: Key poses establish important moments of an action; in-between drawings connect them. Digital tools may interpolate, but artists still control the intended motion.
More drawings alone do not guarantee a convincing movement. 停顿 (“a hold/pause”) and timing affect how motion feels. 中文 原画 often refers to key animation in this production context.

paragraphs.translation: In hand-drawn animation, key drawings establish important poses: for example, crouching before a jump and reaching its highest point.
In-between drawings connect these poses, making the movement continuous.
But smoothness does not depend only on the number of drawings. The length of pauses also changes the rhythm.
Try drawing three poses of a waving hand. Change how long the middle drawing stays on screen, and observe how the feeling changes.

quiz.question: Besides drawing count, what changes the feel of an action?
quiz.explanation: 停顿的长短也会改变节奏: the duration of holds changes the rhythm.

stories.title: 连上了，怎么还是没网？
stories.summary: Describe a connection problem clearly instead of just saying “it is broken”.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 连上了 describes connecting to the local network; 能上网 describes reaching internet services. These are related but different checks.
只有…还是…也…？ helps narrow the problem. The dialogue compares devices before deciding what to restart.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: My phone says it is connected, but webpages will not open.

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Is it only your phone, or is the computer offline too?

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: The computer works. Shall I disconnect the Wi-Fi first?

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Yes, then reconnect. Do not rush to reset the router’s settings.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: It works now! Next time I will explain which devices are affected first.

quiz.question: What useful comparison does the friend ask for?
quiz.explanation: Comparing the phone with the computer helps describe the scope of the problem.

stories.title: 同步不等于备份
stories.englishTitle: Sync Is Not the Same as a Backup
stories.summary: Understand copies, deletion sync, and a simple backup principle.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: Synchronization can propagate a deletion. A backup is intended to let you recover earlier data. Different services offer different version-history and recovery features.
The traditional 3-2-1 rule means three copies including the original, two media types, and one off-site copy. Testing recovery matters too; merely seeing an upload finish is not a restore test.

paragraphs.translation: A sync folder is convenient, but deleting a file on one device may also delete it on another.
Backups are for recovering data. Keep versions you can return to, and understand the service’s recovery rules.
One common principle is three copies including the original, two types of media, and one copy in a different location.
Also try restoring a file. Only when you can recover it do you know the backup is useful.

quiz.question: Do three copies mean three backups plus the original?
options: No, three total including the original
quiz.explanation: 包括原件共三份 means three copies in total, counting the original.

sources.title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Backing up information

stories.title: 听起来很有道理，也可能是错的
stories.englishTitle: A Convincing Answer Can Still Be Wrong
stories.summary: Use AI to start learning while checking the evidence behind a claim.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: Generative AI can produce plausible but false statements and citations. A confident tone is not evidence.
根据什么？ asks “based on what?”. 查证 means verify. Ask for a source, then open and check it yourself; a requested citation is not automatically a valid one.

paragraphs.translation: AI answers sometimes sound very certain. But a certain tone does not mean the information is correct.
It may produce a nonexistent book or an incorrect date. Even a source link needs checking.
You can ask: “What is this conclusion based on?” Then open the original material and look for supporting evidence.
Treat the answer as a starting point for learning. If you cannot find evidence, keep the question open.

quiz.question: What should you do with a source link in an AI answer?
options: Trust it because it looks official
Open it and check the evidence
quiz.explanation: The article says to open original material and verify whether it supports the claim.

sources.title: NIST: Generative AI Profile — confabulation risk

stories.title: 小齿轮为什么能带动大东西？
stories.summary: Connect gear teeth, rotation speed and turning force.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: For an ideal simple gear pair, a small driving gear turning a larger driven gear reduces output speed and increases output torque. Friction reduces real output; gears do not create energy.
扭矩 is turning effect, not the same as rotation speed. In the example, the twenty-tooth driving gear turns twice for one turn of the forty-tooth driven gear.

paragraphs.translation: Imagine a twenty-tooth gear driving a forty-tooth gear. The small gear is the input.
The small gear turns twice while the large one turns once. The output rotation speed becomes half as fast.
Ignoring losses, output torque becomes twice as large. The mechanism trades speed for torque; it does not create energy.
Real gears have friction. So the actual output is lower than the ideal result.

quiz.question: In the example, how many turns does the small driving gear make for one large-gear turn?
quiz.explanation: 二十齿 drives 四十齿, so the small gear makes two turns per output turn.

sources.title: UC San Diego: Gear ratios, speed and torque

stories.title: 先做一个试试看
stories.englishTitle: Make a Prototype Before the Final Part
stories.summary: Discuss a small prototype and agree what to test before manufacturing.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 原型 is a prototype. A prototype can test one question, such as whether parts fit, without proving strength or long-term durability.
先…再决定 is useful in work discussions: “try this first, then decide”. The dialogue avoids assuming every 3D-printed material behaves the same way.

paragraphs.speaker: Designer
paragraphs.translation: I have designed a phone stand. Shall we make the final version straight away?

paragraphs.speaker: Colleague
paragraphs.translation: Let us make a prototype first. What do you most want to test?

paragraphs.speaker: Designer
paragraphs.translation: Whether the phone fits, and whether it blocks the charging cable.

paragraphs.speaker: Colleague
paragraphs.translation: Then print a small sample first. Measure it after printing; do not only look at the screen.

paragraphs.speaker: Designer
paragraphs.translation: Got it. Test the dimensions first, then choose the material based on how it will be used.

quiz.question: What is the first prototype meant to test?
quiz.explanation: This prototype answers fit questions; it does not prove every other property.

sources.title: Formlabs: Design guide and measured features

stories.title: 为什么一样大却装不上？
stories.englishTitle: Why Matching Dimensions May Not Fit
stories.summary: Learn the difference between a nominal size, variation and clearance.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: A nominal dimension is a target; tolerance specifies permitted variation. Clearance is the gap between mating parts. They are related but distinct.

A round pin and a hole with the same nominal diameter do not automatically slide together. The intended fit, process and measurement determine suitable limits; this is not a universal numerical design rule.

paragraphs.translation: The drawing labels both the hole and the pin as ten millimetres in diameter. Does that mean they must fit?
Not necessarily. Real manufacturing produces variation. Tolerance specifies the permitted range of dimensions.
If the pin is slightly large and the hole slightly small, they may jam. A sliding fit needs suitable clearance.
First define the use, then choose the fit and measure the actual parts. Do not copy one gap dimension for every material.

quiz.question: What does tolerance specify?
options: A guarantee that every fit slides
quiz.explanation: 公差规定允许的尺寸范围 means tolerance specifies an allowed dimensional range.

sources.title: Formlabs: Design guide and measured features

stories.title: 这张图准备用在哪里？
stories.summary: Clarify use, size, revisions and timing before creative work begins.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 请问… and 麻烦你… are useful polite openers. 用在哪里？ asks about the intended use, which can affect size, file delivery and permission needs.
修改范围 means the scope of revisions. Confirm the brief together; the example is a communication practice, not a price quote or legal agreement.

paragraphs.speaker: Client
paragraphs.translation: I would like an illustration. May I ask what information you need?

paragraphs.speaker: Artist
paragraphs.translation: Where will the image be used? Is it a personal avatar or a commercial poster?

paragraphs.speaker: Client
paragraphs.translation: A personal avatar. I will send reference images, but I do not want a direct copy.

paragraphs.speaker: Artist
paragraphs.translation: Okay. Let us confirm the dimensions, deadline and scope of revisions.

paragraphs.speaker: Client
paragraphs.translation: Please show me the sketch first. We can agree on the direction before you add colour.

quiz.question: What should be confirmed before colouring?
quiz.explanation: 确认方向后再上色 means agree on the direction, then colour.

stories.title: 放大以后为什么变糊？
stories.englishTitle: Pixels, Paths and a Blurry Logo
stories.summary: Learn why a photo and a vector logo scale differently.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: Raster images store pixels; vector graphics describe shapes mathematically. Vector artwork remains scalable until it is rasterized for a particular output.
An SVG can contain embedded raster images too; a filename alone does not guarantee every part is vector. Adding pixels to a photo cannot automatically recover original detail that was never recorded.

paragraphs.translation: A photograph is usually a raster image made of pixels. Enlarging it greatly may reveal blocks or blur.
Vector graphics describe lines and shapes mathematically. Resizing the artwork recalculates those shapes.
This makes vector artwork suitable for logos in different sizes. But exporting a small raster image does not preserve unlimited scalability.
Before delivering a file, ask whether it is for a screen or print. Then confirm the dimensions and file type.

quiz.question: Why can vector artwork scale cleanly?
quiz.explanation: Vectors describe shapes rather than fixing the artwork to one pixel grid.

stories.title: 柔光不只是把灯调暗
stories.englishTitle: Soft Light Is More Than a Dimmer Switch
stories.summary: Learn why shadow edges depend on the apparent size of a light source.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: A source that appears larger from the subject generally produces softer shadow transitions. Relative size matters: the same source appears smaller when moved farther away.
Brightness and softness are different properties. This comparison changes one condition at a time, which makes the visual effect easier to learn.

paragraphs.translation: In a portrait, soft light usually gives a more gradual transition at a shadow’s edge. It does not simply mean dim light.
From the subject’s position, a light source that looks larger usually produces softer light.
A large window can serve as a large light source. Moving away from it changes its apparent size.
Place the same object at different distances from the window. Keep the camera angle as consistent as possible and compare the shadow edges.

quiz.question: What most directly affects the softness discussed here?
options: The apparent size of the source
quiz.explanation: The light source’s apparent size from the subject affects the transition at shadow edges.

sources.title: Nikon: Portrait and wedding lighting guide

stories.title: 马上到，是多快到？
stories.summary: Use casual chat phrases while giving a genuinely useful arrival time.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 马上到 means “I’ll be there very soon”; it is vague. Add an honest estimate such as 还有十分钟. 在路上 means “on the way”.

收到 is a concise acknowledgement; 稳了 casually means “we’re set / looking good”. These are informal expressions, not promises that nothing can go wrong. 哈哈 marks laughter; it may soften the tone but does not replace an apology.

paragraphs.speaker: Group
paragraphs.translation: Where are you? We are already at the entrance.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Sorry, I am still on the way. About ten more minutes—not immediately!

paragraphs.speaker: Group
paragraphs.translation: Got it. We will grab a table first. Message us when you arrive.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: I am at the entrance now. Where are you sitting?

paragraphs.speaker: Group
paragraphs.translation: By the window. We have a seat for you—we are set!

quiz.question: Which message gives the most useful arrival information?
quiz.explanation: 大概还有十分钟 gives a concrete estimate rather than a vague 马上到.

stories.title: 看完评测，我被种草了
stories.englishTitle: When a Camera Review Makes You Want One
stories.summary: Recognise shopping slang and ask what you actually need.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 种草 zhòngcǎo literally means planting grass; online it can mean making someone want a product or becoming interested in one. 被种草了 means “I’ve been tempted”.

拔草 is context-dependent: it can mean losing the desire to buy, or finally buying something to satisfy that desire. This conversation explicitly uses 不想买了 to mean “I no longer want it”. 安利 is a casual verb for enthusiastically recommending something.

practice.e: remove or satisfy a buying desire; context matters

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: After watching the review, I really want this camera. I have been tempted!

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: What does the reviewer recommend about it? What will you mainly photograph?

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Travel and cars. But the body and lens together look quite heavy.

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Then borrow one to try first. Also check whether you really need that feature.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: I have lost the desire to buy it for now. It is not bad; it just does not suit me.

tokens.e: it is not that it is bad

quiz.question: What does 拔草了 mean in this specific conversation?
options: The speaker no longer wants to buy it
quiz.explanation: The next phrase, 不想买了, makes the intended meaning explicit.

sources.title: People’s Daily: 种草 and product reviews

stories.title: 破防和上头，不是一回事
stories.summary: Understand emotional internet expressions through anime and hobbies.

coach.title: Learn something new
notes: 破防 pòfáng comes from breaking a defence. Online it can describe being emotionally overwhelmed, moved or upset; context decides the tone. It does not always mean anger.
上头 shàngtóu can mean being carried away or hooked. It can also describe alcohol effects in other contexts. Both are casual; 感动 and 入迷 are clearer alternatives when you need a more neutral expression.

paragraphs.translation: A touching scene can make someone say, “That got me emotional.” The 破防 here is not anger.
In an argument, the same expression may describe someone becoming upset. You need to read the context.
“I am hooked on this anime” means being engrossed and unable to stop watching. It is a different feeling.
These are suitable for casual chats among friends. In a more formal explanation, say “I was moved” or “I was engrossed”.

quiz.question: Which expression means “hooked on this anime” here?
quiz.explanation: 太上头了 describes being carried away or hooked in this context.

sources.title: Chinese annual terms: emotional uses of 破防

stories.title: 不想卷，也不是不想学
stories.englishTitle: Learning Without Joining the Rat Race
stories.summary: Discuss pressure without assuming everyone means the same thing by slang.

coach.title: Use it in conversation
notes: 内卷 nèijuǎn commonly describes exhausting competition with little added benefit; it is not a synonym for all hard work. 躺平 tǎngpíng describes stepping back from pressure, sometimes seriously and sometimes jokingly.
These words carry attitudes and can sound judgmental when applied to someone else. Ask 你说的…是什么意思？ to clarify, and use a neutral alternative such as 我想按自己的节奏学习.

practice.e: step back from pressure / lie flat (slang)

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Everyone is comparing how many courses they have finished. It feels like a rat race.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: What do you mean by 内卷—too much learning, or pressure from comparing?

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: The latter. I want to lie flat today, haha.

paragraphs.speaker: You
paragraphs.translation: Do you mean a rest, or that you do not want to learn any more?

paragraphs.speaker: Friend
paragraphs.translation: Just a break! I still want to learn how to draw cars, at my own pace.

quiz.question: What does the friend mean by 躺平 today?
options: Take a short break from comparison pressure
quiz.explanation: The friend clarifies 只是歇一会儿—just a short break. Context matters.

sources.title: Ministry of Education campus discussion: 内卷 and 躺平
